correctness.rationale: Full algebraic proof: BB^T=delta I+lambda J and full row rank; marked-point adjacency span W+B^TW has dimension 2(t+1); strict absorption on bright eigenmodes ensures limit equals orthogonal projection; point coordinates yield 1 or 1/s; block coordinates yield row-space leverage v/b minus centered-incidence variance u(s-u)/(s delta). Verified in 244 subsets and 6936 sites across seven symmetric/nonsymmetric designs, with 150 symbolic projector tests and 20 direct evolution tests (worst projector discrepancy 1.110e-15). Finite tests do not prove the general assertion; the given proof does.

originality.rationale: After comparison by implication against the general Krylov transport framework of Novo et al. (2014), the full spectral and multiple-marked coherent-search analysis of Lugão and Portugal (2023), and the full single-site trap treatment of Razzoli et al. (2020/2021), no inspected antecedent entails the exact non-Hermitian three-or-more point-sink law for arbitrary balanced 2-designs. The previously available two-sink affine-plane case is strictly narrower. Deduplication is best-effort and historical priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: A specialized earlier graph control or absorbing-chain theorem might imply the formula without using design terminology.
The 2023 symmetric-design spectral projectors contain ingredients from which parts of the special symmetric case can be rederived, but they do not state the absorptive quantity or nonsymmetric case.
The 2003 absorbing-walk full text was not inspected; its accessible abstract describes a different discrete-time line/hypercube setting.
Search coverage and accessible-history deduplication cannot prove universal historical priority.

value.rationale: The exact block-side Fisher-gap v/b rules out perfect absorption on every nonsymmetric balanced design irrespective of trap number/location, while symmetric designs admit an incidence-defined perfect-capture criterion. The Fano triple example separates collinear and noncollinear sink placements despite an identical global capture average; this quantifies a nontrivial geometric dark-state effect on infinite families of natural quantum networks.
